record.context_brief: Geometry of the foliated manifold of deformed exponential families
record.original_question: If M is the foliated statistical manifold obtained by taking the union of the leaves M_lambda of lambda-exponential families, can M itself be equipped with a natural geometric structure that is useful for statistical inference?

evidence.quote: Can we equip M with a natural geometric structure that is useful for statistical inference?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a smooth deformation function $\lambda$ and, for each admissible parameter value $\lambda$, let $M_\lambda$ denote the statistical manifold of a $\lambda$-exponential family, i.e. a parametric family of probability densities of the form
$$p(x;\theta) = \exp_\lambda\!\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n \theta^i F_i(x) - \psi(\theta)\Big),$$
where $\exp_\lambda$ is the deformed (lambda-)exponential, $F_1,\dots,F_n$ are fixed sufficient statistics, $\theta=(\theta^i)$ ranges over a natural parameter domain, and $\psi$ is the normalizing potential. Each leaf $M_\lambda$ carries its own deformed information-geometric structure (a Riemannian metric and a pair of dual affine connections induced by the deformation $\lambda$).

Form the disjoint union
$$M = \bigsqcup_\lambda M_\lambda,$$
viewed as a foliated manifold whose leaves are the individual $\lambda$-exponential families.

Question: Does $M$ admit a natural geometric structure (for instance a Riemannian metric, a (possibly dualistic) affine connection, a Hessian or contact structure, or a foliated information-geometric structure) that
(i) restricts on each leaf $M_\lambda$ to the deformed information geometry of the $\lambda$-exponential family, and
(ii) is genuinely useful for problems of statistical inference across leaves (such as estimation, model selection, or hypothesis testing involving the deformation parameter $\lambda$)?

Provide such a structure and establish its inferential utility, or prove that no such canonical structure exists.
artifact.category_tag: Information geometry of deformed exponential families
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on deformed/λ-exponential families and their information geometry (Hessian, dually-flat, conformal, and κ-exponential structures) is active, and recent work studies canonical foliations of statistical manifolds whose leaves are exponential-type models. However, no source identifies a definitive canonical geometric structure on the total foliated manifold M = ⊔_λ M_λ together with established inferential applications. The question appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Canonical foliations of statistical manifolds with statistical models
status_evidence.snippet: Every compact statistical manifold admits a singular foliation whose leaves carry statistical model structures pertaining to exponential families.
status_evidence.claim: Foliated structures on statistical manifolds with exponential-family leaves are an active research topic, but the specific question on M = ⊔ M_λ for λ-exponential families is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Hessian structures on deformed exponential families and their conformal structures
status_evidence.snippet: Deformed exponential family manifolds carry invariant and flat geometries with deformed entropies and divergences.
status_evidence.claim: Per-leaf deformed geometries are well studied, but a canonical inference-useful structure on the total foliated manifold is not established.

status_evidence.title: Information Geometry of κ-Exponential Families
status_evidence.snippet: κ-deformed exponential families admit dually-flat, Hessian and Legendre structures.
status_evidence.claim: Geometry on individual deformed-exponential leaves is known; the cross-leaf structure remains open.
